Scope This Regulation applies to the emission of gaseous pollutants and the energy efficiency in terms of fuel consumption of positive-ignition engines of vehicles of categories L3, L4 and L5.

title: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Approval of a vehicle_ " means the approval of a vehicle type with regard to the limitation of the emission of gaseous pollutants from the engine;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Vehicle type_ " means a category of power-driven vehicles which do not differ in such essential respects as: 2.2.1. the equivalent inertia determined in relation to the reference weight as described in annex 7, appendix 4, to this Regulation, and 2.2.2. the engine and vehicle characteristics as defined in Annex 1 items 1-4 and Annex 2 to this regulation;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: “ _Engine crankcase_ " means the spaces in or external to an engine which are connected to the oil sump by internal or external ducts through which gases and vapours can escape;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Air intake system_ " means a system composed of components allowing the fresh-air charge or air-fuel mixture to enter the engine and includes, if fitted, the air filter, intake pipes, resonator(s), the throttle body and the intake manifold of an engine;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Actuator_ " means a converter of an output signal from a control unit into motion, heat or other physical state in order to control the powertrain, engine(s) or drive train;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Boost control_ " means a device to control the boost level produced in the induction system of a turbocharged or super-charged engine;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Carburettor_ " means a device that blends fuel and air into a mixture that can be combusted in a combustion engine;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Catalytic converter_ " means an emission pollution-control device which converts toxic by-products of combustion in the exhaust of an engine to less toxic substances by means of catalysed chemical reactions;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _CO2 emissions_ " means carbon dioxide;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Cold-start device_ " means a device that temporarily enriches the air/fuel mixture of the engine, or any device or means which can assist to start the engine;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Defeat device_ " means any element of design which senses temperature, vehicle speed, engine rotational speed, drive gear, manifold vacuum or any other parameter for the purpose of activating, modulating, delaying or deactivating the operation of any part of the emission control and exhaust after-treatment system that reduces the effectiveness of the emission control system under conditions which may reasonably be expected to be encountered in normal vehicle operation and use. Such an element of design may not be considered a defeat device if: (a) The need for the device is justified in terms of protecting the engine against damage or accident and for safe operation of the vehicle; or (b) The device does not function beyond the requirements of engine starting; or (c) Conditions are substantially included in the Type I test procedures;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Drive train_ " means the part of the powertrain downstream of the output of the Propulsion unit(s) that consists if applicable of the torque converter clutches, the transmission and its control, either a drive shaft or belt drive or chain drive, the differentials, the final drive, and the driven wheel tyre (radius);

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Drive train control unit_ " means the on-board computer that partly or entirely controls the drive train of the vehicle;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Driver mass_ " means the nominal mass of a driver that shall be 75 kg;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Electronic throttle control_ " (ETC) means the control system consisting of sensing of driver input via the accelerator pedal or handle, data processing by the control unit(s), resulting actuation of the throttle and throttle position feedback to the control unit in order to control the air charge to the combustion engine;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Engine and vehicle characteristics_ ": Subject to the provisions of paragraph 1.1. of Appendix 3 to Annex 7, the engine and vehicle characteristics as defined in Annex 1 to this Regulation;"

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Engine capacity_ " means: (a) For reciprocating piston engines, the nominal engine swept volume(1) ; (b) For rotary-piston (Wankel) engines, double the nominal engine swept volume; (1) Engine displacement shall be calculated using pi = 3.1416, and bore and stroke dimensions shall be rounded to the nearest tenth of a mm.

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Engine control unit_ " means an on-board computer that partly or entirely controls the engine(s) and all emission related devices / systems of the vehicle;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Equivalent inertia_ " determined in relation to the reference mass as defined in 2.36. to this paragraph;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Exhaust emissions_ " means emissions of gaseous pollutants and particulate matter from the tailpipe;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) system_ " means a part of the exhaust gas flow led back to the combustion chamber of an engine in order to lower the combustion temperature;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Forced Induction System_ " is the process of delivering compressed air / air-fuel mixture to the intake of an internal combustion engine;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Super-charger_ " means an intake air/air fuel mixture compressor run by any means other than engine exhaust and used for forced induction of a combustion engine, thereby increasing propulsion unit performance;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Turbocharger_ " means an exhaust gas turbine-powered centrifugal compressor boosting the amount of air charge into the combustion engine, thereby increasing the propulsion unit performance;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Fuel consumption_ " means the amount of fuel consumed, calculated by the carbon balance method;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Gaseous pollutants_ " means carbon monoxide (CO), oxides of nitrogen (NOx) expressed in terms of nitrogen dioxide (NO2) equivalence, and hydrocarbons (HC), assuming a ratio of: C1H1.85 for petrol;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Intercooler_ " means a heat exchanger that removes waste heat from the compressed air by a charger before entering into the engine, thereby improving volumetric efficiency by increasing intake air charge density;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Maximum net engine power_ " is the maximum net engine power of the vehicle as declared by the manufacturer, measured in accordance with ISO 4106:2012;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Maximum vehicle speed_ " (Vmax) is the maximum speed of the vehicle as declared by the manufacturer, measured in accordance with ISO 7117:2010;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Parent vehicle_ " means a vehicle that is representative of a propulsion unit family set out in Appendix 8 to Annex 7;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: (Reserved);

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: (Reserved);

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Pollution-control device_ " means those components (hardware or software) of a vehicle that control or reduce emissions;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Positive ignition engine_ " or " _PI engine_ " means a combustion engine working according to the principles of the "Otto" cycle;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Powertrain_ " means the components and systems of a vehicle that generate power and deliver it to the road surface, including the engine(s), the engine management systems or any other control module, the pollution environmental protection control devices including pollutant emissions and noise abatement systems, the transmission and its control, either a drive shaft or belt drive or chain drive, the differentials, the final drive, and the driven wheel tyre (radius);

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Properly maintained and used_ " means that when selecting a test vehicle it satisfies the criteria with regard to a good level of maintenance and normal use according to the recommendations of the vehicle manufacturer for acceptance of such a test vehicle;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Propulsion unit_ " means a combustion engine, an electric motor, any hybrid application or a combination of those engine types or any other engine type;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Reference mass (mref)_ " means the unladen mass of the vehicle increased with the mass of the driver (75 kg);

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Scavenging port_ " means a connector between crankcase and combustion chamber of a two-stroke engine through which the fresh charge of air, fuel and lubrication oil mixture enters the combustion chamber;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Sensor_ " means a converter that measures a physical quantity or state and converts it into an electric signal that is used as input to a control unit;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Stop-start system_ " means automatic stop and start of the propulsion unit;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Tailpipe emissions_ " means the emission of gaseous pollutants and particulate matter at the tailpipe of the vehicle;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Unladen mass (mk)_ " means the nominal mass of a complete vehicle as determined by the following criteria: Mass of the vehicle with bodywork and all factory fitted equipment, electrical and auxiliary equipment for normal operation of vehicle, including liquids, tools, fire extinguisher, standard spare parts, chocks and spare wheel, if fitted; The fuel tank shall be filled to at least 90 per cent of rated capacity and the other liquid containing systems to 100 per cent of the capacity specified by the manufacturer;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Useful life_ " means the relevant period of distance and/or time over which compliance with the relevant gaseous and particulate emission limits has to be assured;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Alternative fuel vehicle_ " means a vehicle designed to run on at least one type of fuel that is either gaseous at atmospheric temperature and pressure, or substantially non-mineral oil derived;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Gaseous fuel system_ " means a system composed of gaseous fuel storage, fuel supply, metering and control components fitted to an engine in order to allow the engine to run on LPG, CNG or hydrogen as a mono-fuel, bifuel or multi -fuel application;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Mono fuel vehicle_ " means a vehicle that is designed to run primarily on one type of fuel;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Mono fuel gas vehicle_ " means a mono fuel vehicle that primarily runs on LPG, NG/biomethane, or hydrogen but may also have a petrol system for emergency purposes or starting only, where the petrol tank does not contain more than 2 litres of petrol in case of two- wheeled vehicle and 3 litres in case of three -wheeled vehicle;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _LPG_ " means liquefied petroleum gas which is composed of propane and butane liquefied by storage under pressure;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _NG_ " means natural gas containing a very high methane content;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Biomethane_ " means a renewable natural gas made from organic sources that starts out as ‘biogas’ but then is cleaned up in a process called ‘biogas to biomethane’ which removes the impurities in biogas such as carbon dioxide, siloxanes and hydrogen sulphides (H2S);

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Bi-fuel vehicle_ " means a vehicle with two separate fuel storage systems that can run part-time on two different fuels and is designed to run on only one fuel at a time;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Bi-fuel gas vehicle_ " means a bi-fuel vehicle that can run on petrol and also on either LPG, NG/biomethane or hydrogen;

heading: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation,
text: " _Twinned wheels_ " means two wheels mounted on the same axle which are considered to be one wheel, whereby the distance between the centres of their areas of contact with the ground is equal to or less than 460 mm. For two-wheeled motorcycles, in case the vehicle is equipped with a "twinned wheels- " configuration, the full vehicle structure or part of the vehicle structure shall tilt when turning."

title: Application for approval
text: Application for approval

heading: Application for approval
text: The application for approval of a vehicle type with regard to limitation of the emission of gaseous pollutants from its engine shall be submitted by the vehicle manufacturer or by his duly accredited representative.

heading: Application for approval
text: It shall be accompanied by the undermentioned documents in triplicate and the following particulars: 3.2.1. a description of the engine type comprising all the particulars shown in annex 1 to this Regulation; 3.2.2 particulars concerning the vehicle as shown in annex 2 to this Regulation.

heading: Application for approval
text: A vehicle representative of the vehicle type to be approved shall be submitted to the technical service responsible for conducting approval tests, for the tests referred to in paragraph 5. of this Regulation.

title: Approval
text: Approval

heading: Approval
text: If the vehicle type submitted for approval pursuant to this Regulation meets the requirements of paragraphs 5. and 6. below, approval of that vehicle type shall be granted.

heading: Approval
text: An approval number shall be assigned to each type approved, the first two digits of which shall be the highest number of the series of amendments incorporated in the Regulation at the time of issue of the approval. The same Contracting Party may not assign the same number to another vehicle type.

heading: Approval
text: Notice of approval or extension or refusal or withdrawal of approval or production definitively discontinued of a vehicle type pursuant to this Regulation shall be communicated to the Parties to the Agreement applying this Regulation, by means of a form conforming to the model in annex 2 to this Regulation and of drawings and diagrams supplied by the applicant for approval, in a format not exceeding A 4 (210 x 297 mm) or folded to that format and on an appropriate scale.

heading: Approval
text: There shall be affixed, conspicuously and in a readily accessible place specified on the approval form, to every vehicle conforming to a vehicle type approved under this Regulation an international approval mark consisting of: 4.4.1. a circle surrounding the letter “E” followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval; 4.4.2. the number of this Regulation, followed by the letter “R”, a dash and the approval number to the right of the circle prescribed in paragraph 4.4.1.

heading: Approval
text: If the vehicle conforms to a vehicle type approved, under one or more other Regulations annexed to the Agreement, in the country which has granted approval under this Regulation, the symbol prescribed in paragraph 4.4.1. need not be repeated; in such a case the regulation and approval numbers and the additional symbols of all the Regulations under which approval has been granted in the country which has granted approval under this Regulation shall be placed in vertical columns to the right of the symbol prescribed in paragraph 4.4.1.

heading: Approval
text: The approval mark shall be clearly legible and be indelible.

heading: Approval
text: The approval mark shall be placed close to or on the vertical data plate affixed by the manufacturer.

heading: Approval
text: Annex 3 to this Regulation gives examples of arrangements of approval marks.

title: Specifications and tests
text: Specifications and tests

heading: Specifications and tests
text: The Type Approval Authority shall inform the other Type Approval Authorities of Contracting Parties of the circumstances of each type approval granted under this paragraph. The emissions tests for roadworthiness purposes set out in Annex 5 shall still be required to obtain type approval with regard to emissions under this paragraph.

heading: Specifications and tests
text: The components liable to affect the emission of pollutants shall be so designed, constructed and assembled as to enable the vehicle, in normal use, despite the vibration to which they may be subjected, to comply with the provisions of this Regulation.

heading: Specifications and tests
text: The technical measures taken by the manufacturer shall be such as to ensure that in conformity with the provisions of this Regulation, exhaust gas emissions are effectively limited throughout the normal life of the vehicle and under normal conditions of use. This will include the security of those hoses and their joints and connections, used within the emission control systems, which shall be so constructed as to conform with the original design intent. For exhaust emissions, these provisions are deemed to be met if the provisions of paragraph 5.4.1. of this Regulation and paragraph 8. of this Regulation are complied with.

heading: Specifications and tests
text: Any strategy that "optimises" the powertrain of the vehicle running the relevant test cycles in an advantageous way, reducing tailpipe emissions and running significantly differently under real-world conditions differently than under emission test laboratory conditions, is considered a defeat strategy and is prohibited, unless the manufacturer has documented and declared it to the satisfaction of the responsible authority.

heading: Specifications and tests
text: An element of design shall not be considered a defeat device if any of the following conditions is met: 5.1.2.1.1.1. the need for the device is justified in terms of protecting the engine against damage or accident and ensuring safe operation of the vehicle; 5.1.2.1.1.2. the device does not function beyond the requirements of engine starting; 5.1.2.1.1.3. the operating conditions are included to a substantial extent in the test procedures for verifying if the vehicle complies with this Regulation.

heading: Specifications and tests
text: It shall be possible to inspect the vehicle for roadworthiness test in order to determine its performance in relation to the data collected in accordance with paragraph 5.4.4. of this Regulation. If this inspection requires a special procedure, this shall be detailed in the service manual (or equivalent media). This special procedure shall not require the use of special equipment other than that provided with the vehicle. 5.2. Test procedure Table 1 illustrates the various possibilities for type approval of a vehicle.

heading: Specifications and tests
text:
Positive ignition engine-powered vehicles shall be subject to the following tests: Type I (verifying the exhaust emissions after a cold start); Type II (Tailpipe emission at idling speed); Type VII (energy efficiency). Table 1 **Scope with regard to the propulsion unit and fuel type**

heading: Specifications and tests
text: (Reserved).

heading: Specifications and tests
text: Upon the choice of the manufacturer vehicles with positive ignition engines may be tested with either E5 or E10 fuels.

heading: Specifications and tests
title: Nomenclature
text: Nomenclature

heading: Specifications and tests > Nomenclature
text: Wherever required, values shall be rounded off as follows: When the digit next beyond that last place to be retained, is (a) less than 5, retain the last digit unchanged. (E.g. 1.243 becomes 1.24); (b) greater than 5, increase the last digit by one. (E.g. 1.246 becomes 1.25); (c) equals 5, and there are no digits beyond this, or only zeros, increase the last digit by one, if the last digit is odd (E.g. 1.235 becomes 1.24) and retain the last digit unchanged if it is even (E.g. 1.245 becomes 1.24); (d) equals 5, and there are digits beyond this, increase the last digit by one. (E.g. 1.2451 becomes 1.25).

heading: Specifications and tests > Nomenclature
text: Throughout this document the decimal sign is a full stop (period) and, if used, the thousands separator is a space.

heading: Specifications and tests > Nomenclature
text: Temperature shall be measured in °C. Wherever temperature conversion is required in K for calculation purpose, the following equivalence shall be used, 0°C = 273.15K.

heading: Specifications and tests
title: Description of tests
text: Description of tests

heading: Specifications and tests > Description of tests
text: Type I test (Verifying exhaust emissions after a cold start).

heading: Specifications and tests > Description of tests
text: Figure 2 illustrates the routes for Type I test. This test shall be carried out on all vehicles referred to in paragraph 1. of this Regulation.

heading: Specifications and tests > Description of tests
text: The vehicle is placed on a chassis dynamometer equipped with a means of load and inertia simulation.

heading: Specifications and tests > Description of tests
text: The test is carried out using the procedure of Type I test as described in Annex 4 to this Regulation.

heading: Specifications and tests > Description of tests
text:
Subject to the requirements of paragraph 5.4.1.5. of this Regulation the test shall be repeated three times. The resulting masses of gaseous emissions and the mass of particulates obtained shall be less than the limits shown in Table 5. Table 5 **Limit value**
|Class|Limits (|mg/km) for PI|Engines|
|---|---|---|---|
||CO|THC (HC)|NOx|
|1|2 620|750|170|
|2|2 620|750|170|
|3|2 620|330|220|

heading: Specifications and tests > Description of tests
text: Where the prescribed limits are exceeded for more than one pollutant, it is immaterial whether this occurs in the same test or in different tests.

heading: Specifications and tests > Description of tests
text: When the tests are performed with gaseous fuels, the resulting mass of gaseous emissions shall be less than the limits for petrol-engine vehicles in the Table 5.

heading: Specifications and tests > Description of tests
text: Number of tests

heading: Specifications and tests > Description of tests
text: The number of tests shall be determined as shown in Figure 2. Ri1 to Ri3 describe the final measurement results for the first (No. 1) test to the third (No 3) test and the gaseous pollutant.

heading: Specifications and tests > Description of tests
text:
In each test, the masses of the carbon monoxide, hydrocarbons, nitrogen oxides, carbon dioxide and the fuel consumed during the test shall be determined. Figure 2 **Flowchart for the number of Test Type I** Table 6 **Criteria for number of tests**
||Test|Judgement parameter|Criteria emission|
|---|---|---|---|

(a) Each test result shall fulfil the regulation limit Exhaust emissions may be sampled during preparation tests for Test Type I or during verification tests for Test Types VII but the results of these tests shall not be used for the purpose of exhaust emission certification to satisfy the requirements set out in paragraph 5.4.1.4.

heading: Specifications and tests > Description of tests
title: Type II test (Tailpipe emission test at idling speed)
text: Type II test (Tailpipe emission test at idling speed)

heading: Specifications and tests > Description of tests > Type II test (Tailpipe emission test at idling speed)
text: This test is carried out on all vehicles powered by positive ignition engines, in accordance with the test procedure set out in Annex 5:

heading: Specifications and tests > Description of tests > Type II test (Tailpipe emission test at idling speed)
text: Vehicles that can be fuelled either with petrol or with LPG or NG/biomethane shall be tested in the Type II test on both fuels;

heading: Specifications and tests > Description of tests > Type II test (Tailpipe emission test at idling speed)
text: Notwithstanding the requirement of paragraph 5.4.2.1.1., mono-fuel gas vehicles will be regarded for the Type II test as vehicles that can only run on a gaseous fuel.

heading: Specifications and tests > Description of tests
title: Type VII test (energy efficiency)
text: Type VII test (energy efficiency)

heading: Specifications and tests > Description of tests > Type VII test (energy efficiency)
text: Annex 6 sets out requirements with regard to energy efficiency of L-category vehicles, in particular with respect to the measurements of CO2 emissions, fuel consumption. The requirements laid down in Annex 6 apply to the following tests of L-category vehicles equipped with associated powertrain configurations: the measurement of the emission of carbon dioxide (CO2) and fuel Consumption of L-category vehicles powered by a combustion engine;

heading: Specifications and tests > Description of tests > Type VII test (energy efficiency)
text: The components liable to affect CO2 emissions and fuel consumption shall be so designed, constructed and assembled as to enable the vehicle, in normal use, despite the vibrations to which it may be subjected, to comply with the provisions of Annex 6. The test vehicles shall be properly maintained and used. The emissions of CO2 and fuel consumption shall be measured according to the test procedure described in Annex 4 and Annex 6.

heading: Specifications and tests > Description of tests
title: Emission data required for roadworthiness testing
text: Emission data required for roadworthiness testing

heading: Specifications and tests > Description of tests > Emission data required for roadworthiness testing
text: This requirement applies to all vehicles powered by a positive ignition engine for which type approval is sought in accordance with this Regulation.

heading: Specifications and tests > Description of tests > Emission data required for roadworthiness testing
text: When tested in accordance with Annex 5 to this Regulation (Type II test) at normal idling speed: (a) The carbon monoxide content by volume of the exhaust gases emitted shall be recorded; and (b) The engine speed during the test shall be recorded, including any tolerances.

heading: Specifications and tests > Description of tests > Emission data required for roadworthiness testing
text: When tested at "high idle" speed (i. e. > 2 000 min ⁻ ¹) (a) The carbon monoxide content by volume of the exhaust gases emitted shall be recorded; (b) (Reserved); (c) The engine speed during the test shall be recorded, including any tolerances; (Reserved).

heading: Specifications and tests > Description of tests > Emission data required for roadworthiness testing
text: The engine oil temperature at the time of the test shall be measured and recorded.

heading: Specifications and tests > Description of tests > Emission data required for roadworthiness testing
text: An assessment shall be made based on surveys and studies of production vehicles.

title: Modifications of the vehicle type
text: Modifications of the vehicle type

heading: Modifications of the vehicle type
text: Every modification of the vehicle type shall be notified to the administrative department which approved the vehicle type. The department may then either: 6.1.1. consider that the modifications made are unlikely to have an appreciable adverse effect and that in any case the vehicle still complies with the requirements; or 6.1.2. require a further test report from the technical service responsible for conducting the tests.

heading: Modifications of the vehicle type
text: Confirmation or refusal of approval, specifying the alterations, shall be communicated by the procedure specified in paragraph 4.3. above to the Parties to the Agreement applying this Regulation.

title: Extension of approval
text: Extension of approval

heading: Extension of approval
text: Two-wheeled vehicles Approval granted to a two-wheeled vehicle type may be extended to the same propulsion unit family in accordance with the classification criteria prescribed in paragraph 2. of Annex 7 Appendix 8.

heading: Extension of approval
text: Three-wheeled vehicles Approval granted to a two-wheeled vehicle type may be extended to three-wheeled vehicles using the same engine and exhaust system and using a transmission that is either the same or differs only in respect of the over-all transmission ratios.

heading: Extension of approval
text: Restriction When a vehicle type has been approved in accordance with the provisions of paragraphs 7.1. and 7.2. above, such approval may not be extended to other vehicle types.

title: Conformity of production
text: Conformity of production

heading: Conformity of production
text: Every vehicle bearing an approval mark as prescribed under this Regulation shall conform, with regard to components affecting the emission of gaseous pollutants (reserved) by the engine to the vehicle type approved. The conformity of production procedures shall comply with those set out in the 1958 Agreement, Appendix 2 (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3), with the following requirements set out in the paragraphs below.

heading: Conformity of production
text: The tests of Types I, (reserved) shall be performed, as described in Table 1 to this Regulation. The specific procedures for conformity of production are set out in the paragraphs 8.2.

heading: Conformity of production
title: Checking the conformity of the vehicle for a Type I test
text: Checking the conformity of the vehicle for a Type I test

heading: Conformity of production > Checking the conformity of the vehicle for a Type I test
text: The Type I test shall be carried out on a vehicle of the same specification as described in the type approval certificate. When a Type I test is to be carried out for a vehicle type approval that has one or several extensions, the Type I tests shall be carried out either on the vehicle described in the initial information package or on the vehicle described in the information package relating to the relevant extension.

heading: Conformity of production > Checking the conformity of the vehicle for a Type I test
text: After selection by the Approval Authority, the manufacturer shall not undertake any adjustment to the vehicles selected.

heading: Conformity of production > Checking the conformity of the vehicle for a Type I test
text: Three vehicles shall be selected at random in the series and tested as described in paragraph 5.4.1. of this Regulation. The limit values are set out in paragraph 5.4.1.4., Table 5.

heading: Conformity of production > Checking the conformity of the vehicle for a Type I test
text: If the average emissions of the first two vehicles comply with the requirements laid down in paragraph 5.4.1.4 Table 5 then the production conformity is considered as satisfactory.

heading: Conformity of production > Checking the conformity of the vehicle for a Type I test
text: If the average emissions of the first two vehicles do not comply, the COP procedure continues as follows.

heading: Conformity of production > Checking the conformity of the vehicle for a Type I test
text: If the Approval Authority is satisfied with the production standard deviation given by the manufacturer, the tests shall be carried out according to Appendix 1 of this Regulation. If the Approval Authority is not satisfied with the production standard deviation given by the manufacturer, the tests shall be carried out according to Appendix 2 of this Regulation.

heading: Conformity of production > Checking the conformity of the vehicle for a Type I test
text: The production of a series shall be deemed to conform or not to conform on the basis of a sampling test of the vehicles once a pass decision is reached for all the pollutants or a fail decision is reached for one pollutant, according to the test criteria applied in the appropriate appendix. When a pass decision has been reached for one pollutant, that decision shall not be changed by any additional tests carried out to reach a decision for the other pollutants. If no pass decision is reached for all the pollutants and no fail decision is reached for one pollutant, a test shall be carried out on another vehicle (see Figure 3). Figure 3 **Checking the conformity of the vehicle**

heading: Conformity of production > Checking the conformity of the vehicle for a Type I test
text: Notwithstanding the requirements of paragraph 5.4.1. of this Regulation, the tests shall be carried out on vehicles which have travelled a maximum distance of 100 km after first start at the production line.

heading: Conformity of production > Checking the conformity of the vehicle for a Type I test
text: However, at the request of the manufacturer, the tests will be carried out on vehicles which have been run in a maximum of 1 000 km. In this case, the running-in procedure will be conducted by the manufacturer, who shall undertake not to make any adjustments to those vehicles.

heading: Conformity of production > Checking the conformity of the vehicle for a Type I test
text: If the manufacturer asks to be allowed to conduct a running-in procedure (‘x’ km, where x ≤ 1 000 km), it may be carried out as follows: The tailpipe pollutant and CO2 emissions will be measured at maximum 100 km after first start on the production line and at ‘x’ km on the first tested vehicle (which can be the type-approval vehicle); The evolution coefficient (EC) of the emissions between 100 km and ‘x’ km will be calculated as follows: The value of EC may be less than 1. The subsequent vehicles will not be subjected to the running-in procedure, but their 100 km emissions will be modified by the EC. In this case, the values to be taken will be: The value at ‘x’ km for the first vehicle; The values at maximum 100 km multiplied by the evolution coefficient (EC) for the subsequent vehicles.

heading: Conformity of production > Checking the conformity of the vehicle for a Type I test
text: As an alternative to this procedure, the vehicle manufacturer can use a fixed EC of 0.92 and multiply all values of tailpipe pollutant and CO2 emissions measured at zero km by this factor.

heading: Conformity of production > Checking the conformity of the vehicle for a Type I test
text: All these tests shall be conducted with commercial fuel. However, at the manufacturer's request, the reference fuels described in Annex7 Appendix2 may be used.

title: Penalties for non-conformity of production
text: Penalties for non-conformity of production

heading: Penalties for non-conformity of production
text: The approval granted in respect of a vehicle type pursuant to this Regulation may be withdrawn if the requirements laid down in paragraph 8.1. are not complied with or if the vehicle or vehicles taken fail to pass the tests prescribed in paragraph 8.2. above.

heading: Penalties for non-conformity of production
text: If a Party to the Agreement applying this Regulation withdraws an approval it has previously granted, it shall forthwith so notify the other Contracting Parties applying this Regulation, by means of a copy of the approval form bearing at the end, in large letters, the signed and dated annotation "APPROVAL WITHDRAWN”.

Production definitively discontinued If the holder of the approval completely ceases to manufacture a vehicle type under this Regulation, he shall inform thereof the authority which granted the approval. Upon receiving the relevant communication that authority shall inform the other Parties to the Agreement which apply this Regulation thereof by means of a copy of the approval form bearing at the end, in large letters, the signed and dated annotation "PRODUCTION DISCONTINUED".

Names and addresses of technical services responsible for conducting approval tests, and of administrative departments The Parties to the Agreement applying this Regulation shall communicate to the United Nations Secretariat the names and addresses of the technical services responsible for conducting approval tests and of the administrative departments which grant approval and to which forms certifying approval or extension or refusal or withdrawal of approval, issued in other countries, are to be sent.

title: Transitional provisions
text: Transitional provisions

heading: Transitional provisions
text: As from the official date of entry into force of the 02 series of amendments, no Contracting Parties applying this Regulation shall refuse to grant or refuse to accept type approvals under this Regulation as amended by the 02 series of amendments.

heading: Transitional provisions
text: Contracting Parties applying this Regulation may grant type approvals according to any of the preceding series of amendments to this Regulation.

heading: Transitional provisions
text: Contracting Parties applying this Regulation shall continue to grant extensions of existing approvals to any of the preceding series of amendments to this Regulation.

heading: Transitional provisions
text: Approvals granted under this Regulation before the entry into force of the 02 series of amendments and all extensions of such approvals, including those granted subsequently under a preceding series of amendments to this Regulation, shall remain valid indefinitely. If the type of vehicle of category L3, L4 and L5 type approved under the preceding series of amendments meets the requirements of this Regulation as amended by the 02 series of amendments, the Contracting Party which granted the approval shall so notify the other Contracting Parties applying this Regulation.

heading: Transitional provisions
text: No Contracting Party applying this Regulation shall refuse national type approval of a type of vehicle of category L3, L4 and L5 type approved under the 02 series of amendments to this Regulation or meeting the requirements thereof.

heading: Transitional provisions
text: As from two years from the entry into force of this series, Contracting Parties applying this Regulation may refuse first national registration (first entry into service) of a type of vehicle of category L3, L4 and L5 which does not meet the requirements of the 02 series of amendments to this Regulation. title: Introduction

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Introduction
text: This Annex provides a harmonized method for the determination of the levels of gaseous pollutant emissions (reserved) collected at the tailpipe, the emissions of carbon dioxide and is referred to in Annex 6. to determine the energy efficiency in terms of fuel consumption of the vehicle types within the scope of this Regulation that are representative for real world vehicle operation.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Introduction
text: The results may form the basis for limiting gaseous pollutants, to report carbon dioxide and the energy efficiency of the vehicle in terms of fuel consumption by the manufacturer within the environmental performance approval procedures in a robust and harmonized way.

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test conditions > Test Type I procedure > Test bench specifications and settings

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test conditions > Test Type I procedure > Test bench specifications and settings
text: Cooling fan specifications as follows:
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test conditions > Test Type I procedure > Test bench specifications and settings
text: Throughout the test, a variable-rotation speed cooling blower (fan) shall be positioned in front of the vehicle so as to direct the cooling air onto it in a manner that simulates actual operating conditions. The blower rotation speed shall be such that, within the operating range of 10 to 50 km/h, the linear velocity of the air at the blower outlet is within ±5 km/h of the corresponding roller speed (from which the actual vehicle speed is calculated). At the range of over 50 km/h, the linear velocity of the air shall be within ±10 percent. At a desired vehicle speed of less than 10 km/h, air velocity may be zero.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test conditions > Test Type I procedure > Test bench specifications and settings
text: The air velocity referred to in paragraph 3.4.2.5.1. shall be determined as an averaged value of nine measuring points which are located at the centre of each rectangle dividing the whole of the blower outlet into nine areas (dividing both horizontal and vertical sides of the blower outlet into three equal parts). The value at each of the nine points shall be within 10 percent of the average of the nine values.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test conditions > Test Type I procedure > Test bench specifications and settings
text: The blower outlet shall have a cross-section area of at least 0.4 m2 and the bottom of the blower outlet shall be between 5 and 20 cm above floor level. The blower outlet shall be perpendicular to the longitudinal axis of the vehicle, between 30 and 45 cm in front of its front wheel. The device used to measure the linear velocity of the air shall be located at between 0 and 20 cm from the air outlet.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test conditions > Test Type I procedure > Exhaust gas measurement system
text: A connecting tube shall be placed between the device and the exhaust gas sampling system. This tube and the device shall be made of stainless steel, or of some other material which does not affect the composition of the gases collected and which withstands the temperature of these gases.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test conditions > Test Type I procedure > Exhaust gas measurement system
text: Positive displacement pump (PDP)
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test conditions > Test Type I procedure > Exhaust gas measurement system
text: A positive displacement pump (PDP) full flow exhaust dilution system satisfies the requirements of this Annex by metering the flow of gas through the pump at constant temperature and pressure. The total volume is measured by counting the revolutions made by the calibrated positive displacement pump. The proportional sample is achieved by sampling with pump, flow meter and flow control valve at a constant flow rate.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test conditions > Test Type I procedure > Exhaust gas measurement system
text: A heat exchanger capable of limiting the temperature variation of the diluted gases in the pump intake to ± 5 °C shall be in operation throughout the test. This exchanger shall be equipped with a preheating system capable of bringing the exchanger to its operating temperature (with the tolerance of ± 5 °C before the test begins.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test conditions > Test Type I procedure > Exhaust gas measurement system
text: A positive displacement pump shall be used to draw in the diluted exhaust mixture. This pump shall be equipped with a motor with several strictly controlled uniform rotation speeds. The pump capacity shall be large enough to ensure the intake of the exhaust gases. A device using a critical-flow venturi (CFV) may also be used.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test conditions > Test Type I procedure > Exhaust gas measurement system
text: A device (T) shall be used for the continuous recording of the temperature of the diluted exhaust mixture entering the pump.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test conditions > Test Type I procedure > Exhaust gas measurement system
text: Two gauges shall be used, the first to ensure the pressure depression of the dilute exhaust mixture entering the pump relative to atmospheric pressure, and the second to measure the dynamic pressure variation of the positive displacement pump.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test conditions > Test Type I procedure > Exhaust gas measurement system
text: Critical flow venturi (CFV)
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test conditions > Test Type I procedure > Exhaust gas measurement system
text: The use of a CFV for the full flow exhaust dilution system is based on the principles of flow mechanics for critical flow. The variable mixture flow rate of dilution and exhaust gas is maintained at sonic velocity that is inversely proportional to the square root of the gas temperature and directly proportional to gas pressure. Flow is continually monitored, computed and integrated throughout the test.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test conditions > Test Type I procedure > Exhaust gas measurement system
text: The use of an additional critical flow sampling venturi ensures the proportionality of the gas samples taken from the dilution tunnel. As both pressure and temperature are equal at the two venturi inlets, the volume of the gas flow diverted for sampling is proportional to the total volume of diluted exhaust gas mixture produced.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test conditions > Test Type I procedure > Exhaust gas measurement system
text: A CFV shall measure the flow volume of the diluted exhaust gas.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test conditions > Test Type I procedure > Exhaust gas measurement system
text: A probe shall be located near to, but outside, the gas-collecting device, to collect samples of the dilution air stream through a pump, a filter and a flow meter at constant flow rates throughout the test.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test conditions > Test Type I procedure > Exhaust gas measurement system
text: A sample probe pointed upstream into the dilute exhaust mixture flow, upstream of the positive displacement pump, shall be used to collect samples of the dilute exhaust mixture through a pump, a filter and a flow meter at constant flow rates throughout the test. The minimum sample flow rate in the sampling devices described in paragraph 3.4.3.5. shall be at least 150 litre/hour.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test conditions > Test Type I procedure > Exhaust gas measurement system
text: Three-way valves shall be used on the sampling system described in paragraphs 3.4.3.5. and 3.4.3.6. to direct the samples either to their respective bags or to the outside throughout the test.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test conditions > Test Type I procedure > Exhaust gas measurement system
text: Gas-tight collection bags
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test conditions > Test Type I procedure > Exhaust gas measurement system
text: For dilution air and dilute exhaust mixture the collection bags shall be of sufficient capacity not to impede normal sample flow and shall not change the nature of the pollutants concerned. The bag material shall be such as to affect neither the measurements themselves nor the chemical composition of the gas samples by more than ±2 per cent after 30 minutes (e.g., laminated polyethylene/polyamide films, or fluorinated polyhydrocarbons).
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test conditions > Test Type I procedure > Exhaust gas measurement system
text: The bags shall have an automatic self-locking device and shall be easily and tightly fastened either to the sampling system or the analysing system at the end of the test.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test conditions > Test Type I procedure > Exhaust gas measurement system
text: A revolution counter shall be used to count the revolutions of the positive displacement pump throughout the test. Note 2: Attention shall be paid to the connecting method and the material or configuration of the connecting parts, because each section (e.g. the adapter and the coupler) of the sampling system can become very hot. If the measurement cannot be performed normally due to heat damage to the sampling system, an auxiliary cooling device may be used as long as the exhaust gases are not affected. Note 3: With open type devices, there is a risk of incomplete gas collection and gas leakage into the test cell. There shall be no leakage throughout the sampling period. Note 4: If a constant volume sampler (CVS) flow rate is used throughout the test cycle that includes low and high vehicle speeds all in one (i.e. part 1, 2 and 3 cycles), special attention shall be paid to the higher risk of water condensation in the high vehicle speed range.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test conditions > Test Type I procedure > Driving schedules
text: Test cycle WMTC The WMTC test cycles (vehicle speed patterns vs. test time) for the Test Type I consist of up to three parts, as laid down in Appendix 11 to Annex 7. The applicable part of WMTC for each subcategory shall be as per paragraph 3.2. of this section.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test conditions > Test Type I procedure > Driving schedules
text: Vehicle speed tolerances
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test conditions > Test Type I procedure > Driving schedules
text: The vehicle speed tolerance at any given time on the test cycles prescribed in Table A7.App11 is defined by upper and lower limits. The upper limit is 3.2 km/h higher than the highest point on the trace within one second of the given time. The lower limit is 3.2 km/h lower than the lowest point on the trace within one second of the given time. Vehicle speed variations greater than the tolerances (such as may occur during gear changes) are acceptable provided they occur for less than two seconds on any occasion. Vehicle speeds lower than those prescribed are acceptable provided the vehicle is operated at maximum available power during such occurrences. Figure A4/2 shows the range of acceptable vehicle speed tolerances for typical points. Figure A4/2 **: Drivers trace, allowable range**
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test conditions > Test Type I procedure > Driving schedules
text: If the acceleration capability of the vehicle is not sufficient to carry out the acceleration phases or if the maximum design speed of the vehicle is lower than the prescribed cruising vehicle speed within the prescribed limits of tolerances, the vehicle shall be driven with the throttle fully open until the desired vehicle speed is reached or at the maximum design vehicle speed achievable with fully opened throttle during the time that desired vehicle speed exceeds the maximum design vehicle speed. In both cases, paragraph 3.4.4.2.1. is not applicable. The test cycle shall be carried on normally when desired vehicle speed is again lower than the maximum design speed of the vehicle.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test conditions > Test Type I procedure > Driving schedules
text: If the period of deceleration is shorter than that prescribed for the corresponding phase, due to the vehicle characteristics, desired vehicle speed shall be restored by a constant vehicle speed or idling period merging into succeeding constant vehicle speed or idling operation. In such cases, paragraph 3.4.4.2.1. is not applicable.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test conditions > Test Type I procedure > Driving schedules
text: Apart from these exceptions, the deviations of the roller speed (from which the actual vehicle speed is calculated) in comparison to the desired vehicle speed of the cycles shall meet the requirements described in paragraph 3.4.4.2.1. If not, the test results shall not be used for further analysis and the test run shall be repeated.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test conditions > Test Type I procedure
text: Gearshift prescriptions for the WMTC prescribed for the test cycles set out in Appendix 12 to Annex 7.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test conditions > Test Type I procedure > Driving schedules
text: Test vehicles equipped with an automatic transmission
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test conditions > Test Type I procedure > Driving schedules

text: Step 2 - Gear choice for each cycle sample In order to avoid different interpretations of acceleration, deceleration, cruise and stop phases, corresponding indicators are added to the vehicle speed pattern as integral parts of the cycles (see tables in Appendix 11 to Annex 7.). The appropriate gear for each sample shall then be calculated according to the vehicle speed ranges resulting from equations to determine the desired vehicle speeds to shift gears of paragraph 3.4.5.3.1.1. and the phase indicators for the cycle parts appropriate for the test vehicle, as follows: Gear choice for stop phases: For the last five seconds of a stop phase, the gear lever shall be set to gear 1 and the clutch shall be disengaged. For the previous part of a stop phase, the gear lever shall be set to neutral or the clutch shall be disengaged. Gear choice for acceleration phases: gear 1, if v ≤ v1→2 gear 2, if v1→2 < v ≤ v2→3 gear 3, if v2→3 < v ≤ v3→4 gear 4, if v3→4 < v ≤ v4→5 gear 5, if v4→5 < v ≤ v5→6 gear 6, if v > v5→6 Gear choice for deceleration or cruise phases gear 1, if v < v2→1 gear 2, if v < v3→2 gear 3, if v3→2 ≤ v < v4→3 gear 4, if v4→3 ≤ v < v5→4 gear 5, if v5→4 ≤ v < v6→5 gear 6, if v ≥ v4→5 The clutch shall be disengaged, if: (a) the vehicle speed drops below 10 km/h, or (b) the engine speed drops below nidle + 0.03 x (s - nidle); (c) there is a risk of engine stalling during cold-start phase.

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test conditions > Test Type I procedure > Driving schedules
text: The gear choice shall be modified according to the following requirements: (a) no gearshift at a transition from an acceleration phase to a deceleration phase. The gear that was used for the last second of the acceleration phase shall be kept for the following deceleration phase unless the vehicle speed drops below a downshift desired vehicle speed; (b) no upshifts or downshifts by more than one gear, except from gear 2 to neutral during decelerations down to stop; (c) upshifts or downshifts for up to four seconds are replaced by the gear before, if the gears before and after are identical, e.g. 2 3 3 3 2 shall be replaced by 2 2 2 2 2, and 4 3 3 3 3 4 shall be replaced by 4 4 4 4 4 4; In the cases of consecutive circumstances, the gear used longer takes over, e.g. 2 2 2 3 3 3 2 2 2 2 3 3 3 will be replaced by 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 3 3 3; If used for the same time, a series of succeeding gears shall take precedence over a series of preceding gears, e.g. 2 2 2 3 3 3 2 2 2 3 3 3 will be replaced by 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 3 3 3; (d) no downshift during an acceleration phase.

text: The test is designed to determine hydrocarbon, carbon monoxide, oxides of nitrogen, carbon dioxide (reserved) emissions, and fuel consumption while simulating real-world operation. heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test procedures > Test Type I > Calibration of analysers
text:
Analyser calibration procedures Each analyser shall be calibrated as specified by the instrument manufacturer or at least as often as described in Table A4/5. Table A4/5 **Instrument calibration intervals**
|Instrument checks|Interval|Criteria|
|---|---|---|
|Gas analyser linearization (calibration)|Every 6 months|± 2 per cent reading|
|Mid span|Every 6 months|± 2 per cent|
|CO NDIR:|Monthly|-1 to 3 ppm|
|CO2/H2O interface|||
|NOx converter check|Monthly|> 95 percent|
|CH4cutter check|Reserved|Reserved|
|FID CH4response|Reserved|Reserved|
|FID air/fuel flow|At major maintenance|According to instrument manufacturer|
|NO/NO2NDUV:|At major maintenance|According to instrument manufacturer|
|H2O, HC interference|||
|Microgram balance linearity|||
||Reserved|Reserved|
Non-dispersive infrared absorption analysers shall be checked at the same intervals using nitrogen/ CO and nitrogen/ CO2 mixtures in nominal concentrations equal to 10, 40, 60, 85 and 90 per cent of full scale.

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test procedures > Test Type I > Calibration of analysers
text: Each normally used operating range shall be linearized by the following procedure:
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test procedures > Test Type I > Calibration of analysers
text: The analyser linearization curve shall be established by at least five calibration points spaced as uniformly as possible. The nominal concentration of the calibration gas of the highest concentration shall be not less than 80 per cent of the full scale.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test procedures > Test Type I > Calibration of analysers
text: The calibration gas concentration required may be obtained by means of a gas divider, diluting with purified N2 or with purified synthetic air.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test procedures > Test Type I > Calibration of analysers
text: The linearization curve shall be calculated by the least squares method. If the resulting polynomial degree is greater than 3, the number of calibration points shall be at least equal to this polynomial degree plus 2.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test procedures > Test Type I > Calibration of analysers
text: The linearization curve shall not differ by more than ±2 per cent from the nominal value of each calibration gas.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test procedures > Test Type I > Calibration of analysers
text: From the trace of the linearization curve and the linearization points, it is possible to verify that the calibration has been carried out correctly. The different characteristic parameters of the analyser shall be indicated, particularly: (a) Analyzer and gas component; (b) Range; (c) Date of the linearization.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test procedures > Test Type I > Calibration of analysers
text: If it can be shown to the satisfaction of the responsible authority that alternative technologies (e.g. computer, electronically controlled range switch, etc.) can give equivalent accuracy, these alternatives may be used.

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test procedures > Test Type I > Calibration of analysers
text: Detector response optimisation The FID shall be adjusted as specified by the instrument manufacturer. Propane in air should be used on the most common operating range.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test procedures > Test Type I > Calibration of analysers
text: Calibration of the HC analyser The analyser shall be calibrated using propane in air and purified synthetic air. A calibration curve as described in paragraph 5.1.1.2. shall be established.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test procedures > Test Type I > Calibration of analysers
text: Response factors of different hydrocarbons and recommended limits The response factor (Rf), for a particular hydrocarbon compound is the ratio of the FID C1 reading to the gas cylinder concentration, expressed as ppm C1. The concentration of the test gas shall be at a level to give a response of approximately 80 per cent of full-scale deflection, for the operating range. The concentration shall be known to an accuracy of ±2 per cent in reference to a gravimetric standard expressed in volume. In addition, the gas cylinder shall be pre-conditioned for 24 hours at a temperature between 20 and 30°C (293.15K and 303.15K). Response factors shall be determined when introducing an analyser into service and thereafter at major service intervals. The test gases to be used and the recommended response factors are: Methane and purified air: 1.00 < Rf < 1.15 or 1.00 < Rf < 1.05 for NG/biomethane-fuelled vehicles Propylene and purified air: 0.90 < Rf < 1.00 Toluene and purified air: 0.90 < Rf < 1.00 These are relative to a response factor (Rf) of 1.00 for propane and purified air.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test procedures > Test Type I > Calibration of analysers
text: Using the test set up as shown in Figure A4/3 and the procedure described below, the efficiency of converters for the conversion of NO2 into NO shall be tested by means of an ozonator as follows:
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test procedures > Test Type I > Calibration of analysers
text: The analyser shall be calibrated in the most common operating range following the manufacturer's specifications using zero and calibration gas (the NO content of which shall amount to approximately 80 per cent of the operating range and the NO2 concentration of the gas mixture shall be less than 5 per cent of the NO concentration). The NOx analyser shall be in the NO mode so that the calibration gas does not pass through the converter. The indicated concentration shall be recorded.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test procedures > Test Type I > Calibration of analysers
text: Via a T-fitting, oxygen or synthetic air shall be added continuously to the calibration gas flow until the concentration indicated is approximately 10 per cent less than the indicated calibration concentration given in paragraph 4.2.3.4.4.1.1. above. The indicated concentration (c) shall be recorded. The ozonator shall be kept deactivated throughout this process.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test procedures > Test Type I > Calibration of analysers
text: The ozonator shall now be activated to generate enough ozone to bring the NO concentration down to 20 per cent (minimum 10 per cent) of the calibration concentration given in paragraph 4.2.3.4.4.1.1. of this Annex. The indicated concentration (d) shall be recorded.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test procedures > Test Type I > Calibration of analysers
text: The NOx analyser shall then be switched to the NOx mode, whereby the gas mixture (consisting of NO, NO2, O2 and N2) now passes through the converter. The indicated concentration (a) shall be recorded.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test procedures > Test Type I > Calibration of analysers
text: The ozonator shall now be deactivated. The mixture of gases described in paragraph 4.2.3.4.4.1.2. of this Annex shall pass through the converter into the detector. The indicated concentration (b) shall be recorded. Figure A4/3 **NOx convertor efficiency test configuration**
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test procedures > Test Type I > Calibration of analysers
text: With the ozonator deactivated, the flow of oxygen or synthetic air shall be shut off. The NO2 reading of the analyser shall then be no more than 5 per cent above the figure given in paragraph 4.2.3.4.4.1.1. above.
doc_title: Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start

heading: Annex 4 Test Type I, exhaust emissions after cold start > Test procedures > Test Type I > Calibration of analysers
text: The efficiency of the NOx converter shall be calculated using the concentrations a, b, c and d determined in paragraphs 4.2.3.4.4.1.2. through 4.2.3.4.4.1.5. above as follows: The efficiency of the converter shall not be less than 95 per cent. The efficiency of the converter shall be tested in the frequency defined in Table A4/5.
